@copilot Update this existing PR directly with the following consolidated changes. Do not create another PR or work on other PRs.

The user explicitly decided: "I'm not worried about low cardinality here as long as we know they are error codes coming back from the server." Remove the Redis error-prefix allowlist and the formatted-exception-message heuristic based on ". channel:". Accept custom and newly introduced server error codes. The requirement is confirmed server origin, not membership in a fixed list.

Investigate Redisson's protocol decoder and find a safe instrumentation point that captures the prefix from an actual server error reply before failure callbacks complete the instrumentation operation. Redisson's CommandDecoder recognizes RESP '-' error replies, but generic RedisException has no structured error-code field and its message includes diagnostic suffixes; do not infer server origin by parsing those suffixes or arbitrary exception messages. Verify the concrete implementations for the supported redisson-3.0 and redisson-3.17 ranges, including current supported releases. Capture only the first server error-prefix token for error.type, not message text. Preserve retry behavior, completion ownership, asynchronous/batch behavior, and resource cleanup. For errors without a reliably captured server code, preserve the shared canonical exception-class fallback. Do not add an exception-class-to-code enumeration or a cardinality-motivated restriction. Prefer the simplest reliable solution. If no safe compatible decoder integration is feasible, stop and report that blocker rather than substituting another message heuristic.

Update the relevant unit and installed-agent integration tests under instrumentation/redisson. Exercise real WRONGTYPE and custom server error prefixes absent from the current allowlist (for example through a Lua error reply), client-side failures, and successful operations. Verify error.type on spans and db.client.operation.duration, including asynchronous completion and supported baseline/latest versions where relevant to the new decoder integration. Ensure no stale captured code leaks to another operation and no client failure is misclassified as a server reply.

Document briefly the server-reply capture source, any non-obvious lifecycle constraint, and exception-class fallback, with a Redis protocol or upstream decoder reference where useful; do not inventory codes. Follow repository contribution and path instructions. Run narrow formatting and relevant targeted tests in the cloud and report unavailable validation honestly. [Javaagent] Both versioned type matchers omit `BatchCommandData`. Its `tryFailure()` override stores redirect errors without calling `CommandData.tryFailure()` (for example, in Redisson 3.16.8); in 3.52.0 it also does this for `RedisRetryException`. The decoder later completes the batch promise with that exception after the scoped prefix has been restored. Consequently, batch attempts receiving `MOVED`/`ASK`, or newer retry errors such as `LOADING`, record the exception class rather than the server prefix on spans and duration metrics. Include `org.redisson.client.protocol.BatchCommandData` in the capture instrumentation in both `v3_0` and `v3_17`, and cover an overridden batch-failure path in the integration tests.

@copilot Update this existing PR directly with this focused correctness fix.

Fix the new Copilot finding https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-java-instrumentation/pull/20779#discussion_r4340371021.

Both RedisCommandDataInstrumentation type matchers, under redisson-3.0/javaagent and redisson-3.17/javaagent, omit org.redisson.client.protocol.BatchCommandData. Its tryFailure override in Redisson 3.16.8 stores RedisRedirectException without calling CommandData.tryFailure. In 3.52.0 it also stores RedisRetryException, including RedisLoadingException. CommandDecoder subsequently completes the aggregate batch promise after the per-reply decode scope has been restored. The exception therefore lacks its captured server prefix, and both telemetry signals fall back to the exception class.

Include BatchCommandData in failure-capture instrumentation in both splits so the actual override receives decoder-confirmed prefix capture before the scope ends. Preserve constructor/future wrapping behavior and avoid duplicate completion or altered retry decisions. Keep the bounded shared ByteBuffer parsing, dedicated-exception support, virtual-field ownership and cleanup unchanged.

Add focused integration coverage exercising the actual overridden batch-failure path, rather than another generic RedisException batch error. Cover a redirect path such as MOVED or ASK on a supported pre-3.17 version, and the newer retry-error path such as LOADING where supported. Check the literal server prefix on spans and duration metrics, application-visible exception/result preservation, no extra operation completions and no leaked classification on a following success or client failure. Do not introduce message-based provenance or modify application retry behavior to make telemetry pass.

Validate both module splits with relevant unit/integration selectors, pre-3.17 compatibility/latest and current newer dependencies where the overrides exist, plus both affected Muzzle families because injected advice matching changes. Keep all existing dedicated-error, generic-batch and fallback regressions.

Update only this existing PR, directly on its original head branch. Preserve its open draft state and base main. Do not create a new PR as a workaround, retarget or stack this PR, or update another branch. Do not change the PR title or description; the coordinator owns metadata. Do not post comments, replies, reviews, or resolve threads.

Reuse RedisErrorPrefix for lexical extraction. Preserve decoder-confirmed provenance, exception-class or documented _OTHER fallback, omitted error.type on success, agreement between span and duration-metric labels, existing operation names and span boundaries, application messages/results/exceptions, retries and cleanup. Apply the simplifications discussed with the user. First, the two new RedisCommandDecoderInstrumentation classes in redisson-3.0/javaagent and redisson-3.17/javaagent are identical except for their packages. Move their common implementation into redisson-common-3.0/javaagent and register that one implementation from both versioned RedissonInstrumentationModules. Follow existing shared TypeInstrumentation patterns, retaining the same method matching, non-inlined advice, scoped-state restoration on every exit, helper injection and compatibility across both supported ranges.

Second, simplify RedissonErrorCapture.parseServerErrorType by retaining its confirmed '-' marker check, complete CRLF boundary detection, incomplete/replaying-buffer behavior and non-consuming reader-index behavior, then passing the bounded UTF-8 error-line String to the existing RedisErrorPrefix.extract(String). For example, after finding start and replyEnd, use RedisErrorPrefix.extract(input.toString(start, replyEnd - start, UTF_8)). This simplification deliberately trades a full error-line String allocation on the server-error path for removal of the ByteBuffer API introduced by this PR. Remove this PR's new ByteBuffer overload, its now-unused imports, and tests/helpers solely for that overload, provided no other live caller requires it. Inspect all callers first; preserve any independently required shared API rather than breaking another client. Keep the existing String and extractAscii contracts and tests unchanged. Do not add another parser or a Netty dependency to the shared API. This assignment replaces the earlier implementation-specific request to avoid whole-line decoding; it does not change the classification contract.

Third, reduce the duplicated lexical integration-test matrix in AbstractRedissonClientTest and AbstractRedissonAsyncClientTest. Keep case, punctuation, tabs, leading ASCII spaces, unrestricted length and other lexical edge-case coverage once in the shared String parser suite. Retain representative real sync and async server-error tests and all distinct provenance, dedicated OOM/subclass, failed-batch, overridden BatchCommandData redirect/retry, client-side decode failure, success omission and state-leak regressions. Preserve important client-specific Unicode/decoding behavior that a standalone String parser cannot exercise. Do not introduce cross-module test infrastructure just to remove a few repeated assertions, and do not drop distinct lifecycle or compatibility coverage.

Keep raw-reply capture and the exception-attached state handoff. Redisson rewrites some dedicated exception messages, and aggregate batch completion can occur after the decoder scope exits, so neither getMessage() parsing nor thread-local-only completion is an acceptable replacement. Preserve server-confirmed provenance, arbitrary literal server prefixes with ASCII space as the sole token delimiter, no allowlist or length cap, exception-class fallback when no prefix is captured, omission on success, matching error.type on spans and db.client.operation.duration, operation names and span boundaries, exact completion ownership, application strings/results/exceptions, retry decisions and cleanup. Preserve BatchCommandData.tryFailure override coverage in both splits.

Read CONTRIBUTING.md, the knowledge index, and applicable path instructions. Verify the concrete baseline/latest Redisson decoder and completion paths where sharing affects compatibility. Run the narrowest affected spotlessApply tasks directly before targeted behavioral validation, including relevant parser/helper tests, representative real sync/async and batch lifecycle tests, supported baseline/latest selectors and both affected Muzzle families where helper/advice references change. Keep normal caches and existing version coverage; no clean, forced reruns, narrowing latest dependencies, or skipped compatibility checks to hide problems. Report exact commands/results and genuine unavailable-validation blockers in the cloud session result, not a PR testing checklist.

Do not edit this PR's title or description; the coordinator handles any necessary metadata update separately. Do not post comments, replies, reviews, resolve threads, change configuration, add Gradle modules, or make unrelated refactors. Deliver only the simplification with preserved behavior and report any part that cannot safely be completed.

[Javaagent] Consume the scoped prefix before `tryFailure()` can run completion callbacks. In Redisson 3.52.0, `CommandData.tryFailure()` completes its future synchronously. A non-async failure callback can send another command through the same `RedisConnection`; if its `CommandMapper.map()` throws a `RedisException`, `CommandEncoder` calls that new command's `tryFailure()` while the original decoder frame is still active. This method then attaches the original server prefix to the client-side failure, misclassifying its span and duration metric. Clearing the exception's virtual field in `EndOperationListener` does not clear this thread-scoped value. Consume it when attaching it, while retaining the decoder exit's restoration of the previous value, and add a regression test for a client-side failing write issued from a server-error callback.

replies.body: Fixed in baf04368644aeac8d0cd558b6f30605dfc38509c. The prefix is consumed immediately after attachment, before `tryFailure()` can invoke callbacks, while decoder exit still restores the previous scoped value. Commit 7955b9238c9d679bb0b09b5849fe21b187a66e71 adds an installed-agent regression using a real server error and a reentrant mapper failure, with span and duration-metric assertions for both failures and a following success.

@copilot Apply one scoped correctness follow-up to this existing PR directly. The simplification attempt has finished and delivered f581f150631967b43a15ec110f0ad40a1dee1434. Keep its shared decoder instrumentation, bounded UTF-8 String parsing, removed ByteBuffer overload and reduced lexical test matrix intact. Fix the verified finding from Copilot review 5620684007 at https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-java-instrumentation/pull/20779#discussion_r4353388266. In RedissonErrorCapture.captureServerError, the decoder-confirmed prefix remains in currentServerErrorType after attaching it to the server exception. A non-async callback can send a new command through the same RedisConnection while the server-error decoder frame remains active. CommandEncoder calls commandMapper.map inside its encode try/catch; a mapper-thrown RedisException reaches that new command's tryFailure and is incorrectly assigned the earlier server prefix. Clearing only the first exception's virtual field does not remove ambient thread state. This violates the preserved client-failure fallback and no-leak contract.

Use the smallest change to the existing ScopedThreadValue lifecycle, not a new registry or abstraction. Preserve dedicated subclasses, redirects/retry exceptions, application exceptions/results, existing operation boundaries, completion ownership, retry behavior, literal prefix classification, and span/duration-metric agreement.

Add a focused installed-agent regression proving this actual synchronous reentrant path: an actual server-error completion callback issues a command on the same connection whose client-side CommandMapper throws a RedisException. Assert the original operation keeps its server prefix, the reentrant client failure uses canonical exception-class fallback rather than that prefix on both its span and duration metric, completion counts remain exact, and a following success is unclassified. Exercise applicable supported baseline/latest versions without narrowing coverage; version-specific fixture adaptation is acceptable only for actual API differences. replies.body: Fixed in baf04368. `captureServerError` now clears the scoped prefix right after attaching it to the server exception, before `tryFailure` can run callbacks. The decoder exit still restores the previous value. A repeated capture, as with `BatchCommandData` calling `super.tryFailure`, finds no scoped value and leaves the already-attached prefix alone. I added a unit test where a client-side failure captured after the server error stays on the exception-class fallback. The redisson-3.0 unit tests pass. I didn't run the integration tests or Muzzle, and the `spotlessApply` task didn't run.
